summary_en: Left-sided pyelonephritis onset on 01/07/20. admission: 01/16/2020, discharge: 01/26/2020, stay: 09 d 21 h, location: ward, payer: sus. [person] with migraine being followed up at acef. came for a consultation today reporting dysuria, fever, and systemic symptoms for 9 days. in {omitted} 2019 she presented with septic shock with a urinary focus due to left-sided obstructive pyelonephritis. she remained hospitalized at [organization] requiring norepinephrine for 2 days, without the need for orotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation. she underwent treatment with a Double-J stent passage to the left, in addition to meropenem for 10 days, with complete response. on that occasion she presented negative urine and blood cultures. was discharged with outpatient reevaluation by a urology team in {omitted} 2019, with scheduled ureterolithotripsy of a 1.2 cm, 600 hu stone in the proximal third of the left ureter in March 2020. At that time, a pre-anesthetic evaluation was requested, and a follow-up visit was scheduled afterwards. Since discharge, the patient has had 3 episodes of lower urinary tract infection, with symptoms of dysuria, pollakiuria, sensation of incomplete emptying, and hypogastric pain, treated respectively with clavulin 875 mg orally 12/12 h for 14 days, a single dose of fosfomycin, and clavulin 875 mg orally 12/12 h for 14 days, all without the need for hospitalization and with improvement of symptoms. On 01/01/20, a new episode of dysuria, pollakiuria, and sensation of incomplete emptying began. The patient reports not having started antibiotics during this period. On 01/07/20, she began to have a fever of 38.5° and 39°, choosing to seek care at [organization]. She underwent a urine test collection 1, checked on 01/08/20, and was then referred to the city's emergency care unit. On 01/09/20, a single dose of fosfomycin was prescribed and released, however, due to continued fever, with the onset of chills and pain in the lower back and left flank, she follow-up appointmented to the emergency care unit, where she was then prescribed ciprofloxacin 500 mg orally 12/12 h. She reports that since 01/11/20 she has been using ciprofloxacin, without fever, but her general condition continues to decline, nausea, chills, with episodes of vomiting on January 14th and 15th, in addition to severe pain in the lower back and left flank, causing her to lie in the left lateral decubitus position. continues to complain of hypogastric pain, dysuria, pollakiuria, sensation of incomplete emptying. Heart rate: 80 beats per minute, blood pressure: 120x70 mmHg, saturation: 98%, room air, respiratory rate: 18 inspirations per minute, obese, good general condition, afebrile, normal color, alert, cooperative. Cardiac auscultation: regular heart rhythm in 2t, no murmurs auscultation. Respiratory auscultation: vesicular breath sounds without adventitious sounds, no effort, no pain. Abdominal palpation: peripheral perfusion and pulses preserved, no edema. Cultures: urine culture 01/16 70,000 candida albicans multis. Blood culture 01/16 1 sample of micrococcus sp. Urine culture 01/21 negative. Double-J stent exchange on the left 01/18/20. Urine culture for collection 7 days before urological procedure. Lithotripsy to be scheduled by urology team at outpatient follow-up. Follow-up with uro on 03/12/20. Follow-up with cefbot neurocephalea on 05/21/20. Resolution of asymptomatic pyelonephritis.

[person] reported that 2 days after admission, he started feeling unwell, headache and mild myalgia, in addition to coughing, reporting reddish secretion, sensation of chills, reporting an unmeasured fever. he developed dyspnea, even at rest, having difficulty sleeping because of it. he reports that the dyspnea progressively worsened during the night, until he sought care on the day of admission. he denied any other symptoms. in the unit of origin, [person] was admitted eupneic, however with sat02 72% room air. and 85 89% with a reservoir mask, with crackles and wheezing, being administered aerosol with salbutamol, in addition to magnesium sulfate and started oseltamivir, according to the transfer report. [person] admitted to a monitored bed in a coronavirus red room, transferred by [organization], accompanied by [person], saturation 89% with reservoir mask, tachydyspneic, respiratory rate 35 breaths per minute, with use of accessory muscles, glasgow 15. it was decided to proceed with orotracheal intubation, [person] with difficult airway, successfully {omitted} by the anesthesiology team, with use of videolaryngoscopy and a 7.5 tube. sedation and neuromuscular blockade were initiated for better coupling to mechanical ventilation. due to suspected diagnosis of pulmonary thromboembolism, unfractionated heparin was started in a pump, already on a therapeutic regimen with ceftriaxone, clarithromycin, and oseltamivir. due to suspected cellulitis in the left lower limb, oxacillin was introduced to the therapeutic regimen on the same day 04/05. After negative PCR for coronavirus and influenza, [person] was transferred to an intensive care unit bed on 05/05, placed in the proning position, with improved Pao2/Fio2 ratio. Attempted again the next day, but without adequate response. Doppler ultrasound of the lower limbs was performed, ruling out the hypothesis of deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary thromboembolism, with transition from heparin to prophylactic. On 07/05, it was decided to exchange the 7.5 tube for a 9 tube with videolaryngoscopy and a changing tube, without complications. Due to difficulty in managing blood pressure levels, Nipride was started on a continuous infusion pump on 05/13, with optimization of oral antihypertensives and successful weaning later. Due to improvement in ventilatory parameters and adequate level of consciousness, extubation was performed on 05/14, successfully. [person] presented bronchospasm after the same, with improvement after clinical measures. After extubation, changes in extrinsic ocular motility were identified, in addition to anisocoria. The hypothesis of pharmacological anisocoria was raised, and a test with 1% atropine was performed, with a response of symmetrical mydriasis and congenital divergent strabismus. In addition, [person] also presents with tetraparesis, secondary to critical patient myopathy. Since 05/15, [person] has been evolving with persistent subfebrile levels 37.5 - 37.7, reaching maximum peaks of 37.9, but continuing to improve clinically. A new infectious screening was performed and central venous access and invasive blood pressure were removed. Due to clinical stability, no use of vasoactive drugs, [person] is comfortable in room air. [person] transferred to [organization] on 05/20. while admitted to the ward, [person] presented a fever of 37.8º C, with no other associated symptoms. A new infectious screening was performed, with no signs of infection in laboratory or radiological tests. Indwelling urinary catheter removed on 05/22. Acute kidney injury Kdigo 3 secondary to sepsis of pulmonary focus Urinary tract infection Intermittent hemodialysis since 04/15. 5. Upper gastrointestinal bleeding due to duodenal ulcer Forrest IIB Local injection of adrenaline performed. 01/05 omeprazole 40 mg IV 12/12h. 6. intestinal constipation. non-contrast abdominal computed tomography: distension of intestinal loops without obstructive factor requiring multiple intestinal lavages. contrast-enhanced abdominal tomography 03/05: slight distension of colonic loops, presence of fecal content in the small intestine. no obstructive factor visible. small volume of free intra-abdominal fluid. findings suggest reduced intestinal motility {omitted}. 7. urinary tract infection, urine with pyuria-like appearance episodes of urinary retention urine culture 23/04: polymyxin-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in ceftazidime avibctam 01/05. 8. decreased level of consciousness to be clarified infectious, metabolic? encephalopathy due to ceftazidime? on 05/05 with progressive worsening of oromandibular automatism, myoclonus in the left side of the body focal seizure? myoclonus of metabolic etiology? computed tomography of the skull 07/05: subcortical hypodensities, moderate microangiopathy, without signs of acute ischemia and without signs of hemorrhage. calcifications in the basal ganglia, which may not have clinical significance. electroencephalogram 08/05: the electroencephalogram was abnormal. the findings of basal activity are compatible with marked diffuse encephalopathy, being more suggestive of toxic, metabolic etiology. by neurology: hypothesis of association of ceftazidime in the presence of acute renal failure as possible etiology. 9. infectious worsening during antibiotic therapy fungal urinary tract infection? bloodstream infection related to the catheter? deviation to the left, subfebrile peaks, decreased level of consciousness on 05/06 in vancomycin 05/07 catheter tip culture 04/26 with growth of staphylococcus aureus we considered the finding as colonizing, however in view of clinical worsening we opted for urinalysis coverage: field taken for leukocytes, urine culture: candida albicans. admission: 13/04/2020, discharge: 13/05/2020, stay: 01 m 04 h, location: ward, payer: sus. history of current illness: [person] brought to this service by [organization], sedated, orotracheal intubation mechanical ventilation agitation scale sedation 5. according to report by the [organization] team and later by family members present, [person] has presented prostration, fever, myalgia and dyspnea on exertion for approximately 07 days. [person] had a long-standing history of worsening productive cough with mucopurulent expectoration in association with general symptoms. He sought care at [organization], where he remained for 2 days for further investigation. This morning, still at [organization], after reversal of atrial flutter by 100J electrical cardioversion, he developed acute respiratory failure and was then subjected to orotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation at the service of origin. Given the associated hemodynamic instability, vasoactive drugs were started, discontinued after a short period, after which [person] began to present arterial hypertension. He continued to show no therapeutic response and died today at {omitted}. Absence of central pulses, silent chest, apnea, absence of pupillary reflexes. Death.

Previous antihypertensives enalapril and carvedilol were reintroduced, however with poor blood pressure control, and hydrochlorothiazide was started on an outpatient basis. He was discharged in good general condition, without complaints of pain, without odynophagia or dysphagia, with outpatient follow-up schedule, new upper gastrointestinal endoscopy in March and maintenance of use.

[person] apresentou níveis pressóricos elevados com necessidade de introdução de nitroprussiato em 15/05. tentado desmame de sedação para extubação, porém [person] apresentava agitação importante mesmo com doses consideráveis de midazolam e precedex. foi admitida no semi intensivo em 16/05 à noite. em 17/05, devido à história de etilismo importante, optado por iniciar lorazepam para manejo de possível síndrome de abstinência alcoólica mantido ceftriaxona e associado clindamicina em 17/05 pela possibilidade de pneumonia aspirativa [person] com leucocitose e picos febris mesmo em uso de ceftriaxona. em 19/05, optado por realizar extubação visto que [person] consciente, aparentemente colaborativa, sem broncoespasmo, em ventilação mecânica por psv e em uso de metilprednisolona há vários dias. no entanto, [person] apresentou taquipneia e esforço respiratorio mesmo em uso de mascara com reservatorio a 10 l/min, apresentava sibilos e principalmente roncos difusos, com ausculta cervical sugestiva de estridor. visto falha de extubação, optado por realizar intubação orotraqueal para garantir ventilação adequada. [person] realizou intubação com bougie, porém [person] manteve dessaturação e evoluiu com atividade eletrica sem pulso. iniciadas manobras de reanimação cardiopulmonar, realizados 4 ciclos com administração de 2 ampolas de adrenalina. [person] retornou à circulação espontanea apos 4 ciclos, com pulsos centrais palpaveis, porem manteve dessaturação. verificada presença de pneumotorax hipertensivo à direita, com melhora dos parâmetros ventilatórios após toracocentese de alívio colocação de dreno de tórax. realizou tomografia computadorizada crânio, cervical e de tórax em 20/05, que evidenciaram enfisema subcutâneo volumoso e imagem inespecífica em brônquio fonte direito. [person] apresentou necessidade de troca de dreno de tórax em 20/05 devido ao mau posicionamento e por não apresentar oscilação. ficou com o dreno de tórax até 22/05, quando foi retirado pela equipe de cirurgia, não apresentando diminuição de ausculta ou piora de parâmetros ventilatórios após. summary_en: seizure status right bronchus injury pneumothorax pneumonia bloodstream infection. admission: 14/05/2020, discharge: 06/05/2020, stay: 22 days 04 hours, location: ward, payer: sus. history of current illness informant entry: [person]: patient last seen well on 10/05/2020, around 9:00 pm. the next day, she was found at 7:30 am by neighbors unconscious, with her tongue bitten off and with urine on her clothes and on the floor. she was taken to the emergency care unit by [organization]. there, reentrant seizures were reported that did not cease even after diazepam and hydantoin. she was intubated due to a decrease in her level of consciousness. after sedation with midazolam and bic fentanyl, the seizures ceased. she developed acute kidney injury, presenting oliguria and dark urine. Report of attempts to wean from sedation, but [person] follow-up appointmented to present signs of a crisis, requiring sedation to be resumed. Due to a fever spike, on 05/11 ceftriaxone was started due to the diagnostic hypothesis of meningitis causing CC and lowering of the level of consciousness. In external examinations, he presented significant thrombocytopenia. [person] has been drinking 1 l of distilled spirits per day for 20 years. [person] reports that for about 5 years he has been presenting memory alteration, with episodes of leaving the stove on and confusing people, with progressive worsening. He has also been presenting falls from his own height, one of the times with traumatic brain injury requiring hospitalization. He does not know whether he required ICU, but does not think he required orotracheal intubation, for about 3 years. He has also been presenting convulsive crises for about 3 years. [person] does not remember whether they started before or after the [organization]. A month ago, [person] presented a similar picture of seizures refractory to medication and also required orotracheal intubation. She was discharged with a prescription for antiepileptics carbamazepine 200 mg 8/8h clonazepam 20 gts/night, but was not taking them. [person] was admitted to the emergency unit, brought by [organization] already intubated with TOT 7.5 fixed at the 25cm rim, and was positioned on the respiratory isolation bed for monitoring. She was admitted in poor general condition, sedated, Glasgow 3T, mydriatic, isochoric, bradyreactive pupils. In orotracheal intubation, ventilation was difficult in the AMB, with tongue edema. After measures for bronchospasm and aspiration of the mucus plug in TOT, there was an improvement in the ventilatory parameters. She presented with shock, requiring norepinephrine, which was weaned on the same day, maintaining a mean arterial pressure of 70. Evolution during hospitalization [person] was admitted to the isolation bed in poor general condition, hypotensive, with a silent chest. She underwent norepinephrine volume replacement, measures for bronchospasm, and airway aspiration with improvement in ventilatory parameters and improvement in hypotension. She underwent laboratory tests that showed acute kidney injury and rhabdomyolysis, and hyperhydration was initiated. A cranial computed tomography scan and cerebrospinal fluid puncture were requested, but due to the platelet count of 9000, cerebrospinal fluid was collected on 05/14 after transfusion of 1 platelet apheresis. A cranial computed tomography scan showed no changes and the cerebrospinal fluid was normal, so [person] was taken to the ER and had her ceftriaxone dose reduced to 1 g 12/12h. Phenobarbital was started on May 15, under the guidance of the neurology department, due to a previous history of seizures. [person] presented high blood pressure levels, requiring the introduction of nitroprusside on May 15. An attempt was made to wean her from sedation for extubation, but [person] presented significant agitation even with considerable doses of midazolam and Precedex. She was admitted to the semi-intensive care unit at night on May 16. On May 17, due to a history of significant alcoholism, it was decided to start lorazepam to manage a possible alcohol withdrawal syndrome, and ceftriaxone was maintained and clindamycin was associated with her on May 17 due to the possibility of aspiration pneumonia [person] with leukocytosis and fever spikes even while taking ceftriaxone. On May 19, it was decided to perform extubation, since [person] was conscious, apparently cooperative, without bronchospasm, on mechanical ventilation by PSV, and on methylprednisolone for several days. However, [person] presented tachypnea and respiratory effort even with the use of a mask with a 10 L/min reservoir. He presented wheezing and mainly diffuse rhonchi, with cervical auscultation suggestive of stridor. Given the extubation failure, it was decided to perform orotracheal intubation to ensure adequate ventilation. [person] underwent intubation with a bougie, but [person] maintained desaturation and evolved with pulseless electrical activity. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation maneuvers were initiated, and 4 cycles were performed with administration of 2 ampoules of adrenaline. [person] follow-up appointmented to spontaneous circulation after 4 cycles, with palpable central pulses, but maintained desaturation. The presence of tension pneumothorax was verified on the right, with improvement in ventilatory parameters after relief thoracentesis and placement of a chest tube. underwent computed tomography of the skull, neck, and chest on 05/20, which showed massive subcutaneous emphysema and nonspecific imaging in the right main bronchus. [person] required chest drain replacement on 05/20 due to poor positioning and lack of oscillation. The chest drain remained in place until 05/22, when it was removed by the surgical team. There was no decrease in auscultation or worsening of ventilatory parameters after that. [person] presented worsening of leukocytosis and fever plateau. New cultures were collected and antibiotic therapy was escalated to meropenem vancomycin on 05/21. The patient progressed well with ventilatory weaning. She was maintained on macronebulization on 05/28 without complications. She had 1 fever spike on 05/27. We removed the indwelling urinary catheter and requested infection screening with blood culture and chest X-ray. Although fever did not recur, worsening of the leukogram was observed. On 05/28, we decided to remove the central venous access in the right subclavian vein with a catheter tip culture. We performed a new puncture of the central venous access in the right femoral vein due to peripheral access failure. [person] was progressing well, without sedation since the morning of 05/27. He presented with hyperactive delirium, which is already improving. He responds well to verbal management with quetiapine. On 06/02, the tracheostomy was replaced with a metal one, without complications. [person] maintained moderate secretion volume via the tracheostomy. On 06/03, he was evaluated by [organization], performed a PAN, and was advised to continue follow-up with speech therapist, and a new case was scheduled for ELT on 08/13. On 06/04, antibiotic therapy with meropenem was completed for a treatment period of d14 for a pulmonary focus, bloodstream. cultures: blood cultures: 05/14: negative 05/20 paired with catheter tip: enterococcus faecalis multis 05/21: negative 05/27: in processing negative so far 05/28 paired with catheter tip: in processing negative so far tracheal aspirate: 05/22: negative urine cultures: 05/15: negative after 48 h of incubation 05/21: negative after 48 h of incubation 05/28: in processing others: cerebrospinal fluid 05/14: staphyloccocus haemolyticus contaminating catheter tip 05/20: enterobacter cloacae sensitive to meropenem catheter tip 05/28: negative. tracheostomy 05/26. follow-up 1 tracheostomy care change to metal cannula no. 05 on 02/04 frequent aspiration maintain follow-up with speech therapist new case at hc [organization] on 08/13. 2 epilepsy advised start of carbamazepine by neurology d0 05/28 weaning from intravenous phenytoin 50 mg every 2 days until discontinuation of current use: 150 100 mg, last reduction on 06/03. 3 hyperactive delirium delirium already improving with use of quetiapine 12.5 25 mg 3 care for sacral ulcer. new case at hc [organization] on 08/13. transfer to backup bed at {organization} performed completion of antibiotic therapy report delivered general guidelines.

summary_en: [person], 69 years old. admission: 07/01/2020, discharge: 12/02/2020, stay: 01 m 05 d 06 h, location: ward, payer: sus. patient admitted to this service with acute abdomen on 07/01/2020. underwent exploratory laparotomy that revealed intrathoracic gastric volvulus, gastric secretion in the thoracic cavity, lesser curvature ischemia with perforation of approximately 2 centimeters. total gastrectomy, end-to-side esophagojejunal anastomosis, roux-en-y reconstruction were performed. and remained under peritoneostomy. evolution with refractory abdominal septic shock, acute kidney injury, and disseminated intravascular coagulation. need for multiple surgical reapproaches due to duodenal fistula. During hospitalization in the intensive care unit, he received broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy, including polymyxin B, meropenem, micafungin, and levofloxacin. An evaluation by the palliative care team was requested, and then. Abdominal pain that had been present for 4 days prior to hospital admission. Blood culture, ascitic fluid culture, and tracheal aspirate were positive for multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae. Stomach necrosis culture was positive for Candida tropicalis. Tracheal aspirate culture was positive for Stenotrophomonas. Ascitic fluid culture was positive for Proteus mirabilis. On January 7, total gastrectomy was performed, esophagojejunal anastomosis was performed at the end of the lateral esophagus, and Roux-en-Y reconstruction was performed. He remained with peritoneostomy. On January 21, tracheostomy was performed, and multiple revisions of the peritoneostomy were performed. [person] developed cardiorespiratory arrest in asystole and death was confirmed at {omitted}, death certificate issued, family welcomed.

On 10/25, he started a soft oral diet with good acceptance, and the nasogastric tube was removed and treatment for pleural tuberculosis was initiated by the attending medical team. A family member states that [person] went to a bar, drank less than usual and, afterwards, sat for hours without communicating with others. [person] noticed a change and contacted [organization]. [person] was admitted to [organization] with the same signs and symptoms. Laboratory tests were requested, which showed acute kidney injury, elevated creatine phosphokinase, and leukocytosis. 500 ml of Ringer's lactate and 2,000 ml of 0.9% saline solution were administered at the origin. Report of indwelling urinary catheter placement at the origin, with minimal diuresis. Family and team reports conflicting regarding the presence or absence of falls. There are no reports of witnessed seizures, current or previous. I admit [person] hemodynamically stable without vasoactive drugs, breathing spontaneously in room air, with no signs of discomfort. Confused and barely able to communicate, with slowed speech and slight tremor in the right upper limb. Poor general condition, flushed, hydrated, anicteric, acyanotic, afebrile to the touch, conscious eupneic, alert, but due to catatonia, assessment regarding degree of orientation, he is impaired. Abdomen: globular, without visible lesions, normotensive, diffuse tympanism. Painless to palpation. No palpable masses. Absence of peritonism. Lower limbs: good peripheral perfusion, without edema, without swelling. External rotation of the left lower limb. Presence of edema in the right ankle, with previous surgical scar. Intermittent hemodialysis. Regarding kidney injury: under joint follow-up with nephrology. Given the history of alcoholism and deficit, I maintain vitb12 5000 mcg/week for 1 month. I maintain dipyrone on a schedule and I stop taking tramadol 50 mg if necessary to avoid drowsiness. [person] is comfortable with analgesia. [organization] continued to be followed and advised not to administer antipsychotics if [person] was agitated due to the risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Benzodiazepines were administered until sedation was achieved and, if necessary, a beeper was administered to [organization]. Report was prepared by the [organization] team aiming to continue bedside treatment at {organization}. The patient sought emergency care with worsening of her general condition. Upon being seen at the emergency care unit, [person] was septic, tachycardic, tachypneic, and hypotensive, with laboratory tests compatible with bacterial infection. She underwent expansion with saline solution and a dose of ceftriaxone, and was then referred to this unit. She denied hospitalization or recent use of antibiotics in the last year. She denied recurrent urinary tract infection or lithiasis. She was admitted to a monitored bed in a clinical stabilization room, awake and oriented, hemodynamically stable, tachypneic on room air, but with no signs of respiratory distress, with good peripheral perfusion. Evolution during hospitalization: initially, antibiotic therapy for sepsis of urinary focus with ceftriaxone was maintained, and a computed tomography scan of the abdomen showed an inflammatory process in the kidneys. She presented hematuria and proteinuria upon admission with a protein/creatinine ratio of 3.48 g. She required supportive renal therapy started on 02/14, with joint follow-up with nephrology during hospitalization, suggesting the need for a renal biopsy after resolution of the infectious condition. On 02/18 [person] presented a disproportionate increase in white blood cells, fever, abdominal pain, and antibiotic therapy was escalated to cefepime. A new abdominal computed tomography scan was performed on 02/18 to investigate a renal abscess, and the absence of an abscess and signs of a bilateral renal inflammatory process were found. After escalation of antibiotic therapy, the general condition improved, the patient remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable. Antibiotic therapy was suspended on 02/28. There was progressive recovery of renal function. Last hemodialysis on 02/21. In addition to urinary changes of hematuria and proteinuria, [person] presented pleural effusion and photosensitivity, and autoantibodies were requested to investigate autoimmune disease and systemic lupus erythematosus. Awaiting the results of tests in processing. Dialysis catheter removed on 02/28. urinalysis test repeated on 02/28. The urinary sediment improved. Chest computed tomography 20/02: bilateral pulmonary consolidations, which may represent atelectasis and/or an infectious inflammatory process. The presence of a possible abdominal focus was excluded by diagnostic paracentesis performed on 10/22, without criteria for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. The presence of Staphylococcus aureus was observed in 02 pairs of blood cultures. A transthoracic echocardiogram was performed, which excluded endocarditis. During hospitalization, [person] presented acute kidney injury kdigo 3. Due to the underlying liver disease, expansion with albumin 1 g/kg was performed for 48 hours for differential diagnosis of hepatorenal syndrome. There was an improvement in renal function, although the baseline creatinine level was not 0.69, and the hypothesis of hepatorenal syndrome was excluded. [person] maintains good urinary output. [person] referred from the emergency care unit in {city} in usb, accompanied by [person]. presenting with a fever of 39 °C for 5 days throughout the day without recurrence, associated with cough with expectoration, without signs of respiratory distress, subjective complaints impaired by cognitive deficit and loss of appetite. In the dialysis service, oral antibiotic therapy was started without improvement. He sought emergency care on 02/06 due to persistent symptoms, and was administered ceftriaxone 2 g intravenously and regulated for this service. {omitted}. [person] was admitted conscious and oriented, initially hemodynamically stable without vasoactive drugs, eupneic saturation 92% with oxygen catheter at 3 l/min, without spontaneous complaints. He denied dyspnea, cough, expectoration, chest or abdominal pain. Afebrile and presenting with usual diuresis and evacuation without pathological products. During hospitalization, [person] became unstable and needed to start norepinephrine 0.12 mcg/kg/min. General tests were requested and [person] was neutropenic. A chest tomography showed posterior consolidations and she was considered to have septic shock with a pulmonary focus and febrile neutropenia. Antibiotic therapy with cefepime and vancomycin was started due to a dialysis catheter. In addition, she started with abdominal pain 1 day ago and was diagnosed with acute hepatitis, and among the possible causes, she had a positive igm for epstein bar virus, and then ganciclovir was started, discussed with hemato. However, due to the history of fever for 5 days and loss of appetite, ns1 was requested, which came back positive. Therefore, dengue was considered the cause of the acute hepatitis and ganciclovir was suspended, discussed with [person]. She was transferred to [organization] on 02/08/2020, and the next day, she developed ulcers in the oral cavity, in addition to psychomotor agitation, with herpetic encephalopathy being suspected and acyclovir being started. Due to persistent oral cavity bleeding and decreased level of consciousness, she was intubated on 02/10/2020. She continued to have oral cavity bleeding and thrombocytopenia. The orotracheal tube was replaced due to the presence of a mucus plug on 02/18/2020. A tracheotomy was performed on 02/20/2020 due to failed extubation with Tobin 200 and cleaning of the nasal and oral cavity with a hemostatic tampon with gelfuan in the nasal cavity and peritracheostomy. On 02/22, she restarted medications to control systemic arterial hypertension and heart failure with enalapril and bisoprolol, with improved ventilatory weaning and she was able to remain on macro since 02/25/2020 8 hours. After admission to a bed in the semi-intensive care unit of [organization], [person] presented a fever which was considered secondary to an abscess in the right upper limb. It was decided to start empirical treatment with vancomycin. The abscess was drained by the orthopedics team on 2/27/2020, with good progress and discharge by the team on 3/4/2020. On 2/28/2020, [person] presented fever and hypotension during the hemodialysis session. Contacted [person] from [organization] and decided to start meropenem for coverage of the pulmonary focus due to the appearance of a new radiopacity in the right hemithorax associated with respiratory distress. On 03/02/2020, [person] presented new fever spikes, associated with clinical worsening and new consolidation in the right hemithorax. Tracheal aspirate culture checked showing meropenem-resistant acinetobacter, discussed with [organization] and then decided to start polymyxin B and gentamicin. The next day, he maintained fever spike and blood culture showed growth of gran-negative bacillus in 8 h acinetobacter, requested the nephrology team to remove permcath. Two days later, a new dialysis catheter was inserted in the right femoral vein on 03/05 without complications. During her stay in semi-intensive care, [person] presented episodes of epistaxis and otorrhea on the right, which were evaluated by the otorhinolaryngologist and showed good progress. [person] was transferred to the [organization] ward on 3/10, where she remained well, under frequent monitoring with speech therapy, progression of diet to oral route, physical therapy, weaning from bipap, tolerating macronebulization well, and managing to keep the tracheostomy occluded since 3/11. Upon admission, anisocoria was described and the patient was normal, with 183,000 platelets, dextrose 178, and blood pressure 150/90 mmHg. Upon admission, computed tomography of the skull showed aspect 10, with no signs of early ischemia, with CT Angiography (CTA) showing occlusion at the origin of the left vertebral column, with reinhabitation in distal V2, without other stenoses or occlusions. It was decided not to thrombolyze due to the clinical picture not suggestive of ischemic stroke and no images that corroborated this diagnosis. Diagnostic hypothesis of convulsive crisis, with a decrease in the level of consciousness in the postictal period, evolving with the need for orotracheal intubation. In the initial infectious-metabolic screening, a urinary tract infection was found and treatment with ceftriaxone was initiated. The patient evolved with rapid recovery of the level of consciousness with weaning from sedation and was extubated, without complications, on 05/29. During hospitalization, the patient presented an episode of deep vein thrombosis in the right upper limb. Treatment was started with enoxaparin 0.75 mg/kg/day, which subsequently evolved to cellulitis in the right upper limb. Treatment was started with oxacillin. He had an episode of multifocal atrial tachycardia that was reversed with amiodarone. The following hypotheses led to hospitalization and discharge: 1. summary_en: Hemorrhagic stroke. admission: 2020-06-05, discharge: 2020-07-09, stay: 01 m 03 d 22 h, location: ward, payer: SUS. [person] 50 years old, previously hypertensive, taking losartan. Upon arriving home from work at around 6:30 pm on 06/05, he began vomiting associated with mental confusion with subsequent hemiparesis. Brought by the SAMU team to [organization] with a windowed ischemic stroke. Upon admission to [organization], [person] was hypertensive, with blood pressure 220x120 mmHg, intarparenchymal hemorrhage, and 43 ml of thalamocapsular intraparenchymal hemorrhage. Nipride was started to control blood pressure. Underwent craniotomy to drain intraparenchymal hemorrhage. Extubated on 06/07. On 06/07, losartan 25 mg 12/12h and hydrochlorothiazide were started, but hypertensive requiring nipride. The patient developed a decrease in consciousness on 06/09 and was reintubated. [person] underwent decompressive craniectomy with a bone flap placed in the abdomen on 06/10. Blood pressure was controlled with nipride. The patient presented with fever on 06/12 and a new infectious screening was performed. Seizure on 06/13, controlled with diazepam and phenytoin attack. Treatment for ventilator-associated pneumonia was started on 06/16, guided by tracheal aspirate culture with growth of Klebsiella pneumoniae sensitive to meropenem. On 06/18, a central nervous system infection was suspected and vancomycin was started, in addition to adjusting the dose of meropenem for the central nervous system. Furthermore [person] remained febrile and with recurrent seizures. CSF was collected on 6/22 with: xanthochromic fluid, 20 cells, 968 red blood cells, 92% lymphocytes, glucose 86, protein 161, chloride 113. Lactate 2.7 [person] with recurrent use of nipride for blood pressure control, but it was observed that vasoactive drugs are only necessary after seizures with rapid weaning. Sedation was maintained since 6/18 due to recurrent seizures. On 6/25, phenobarbital was started and on 6/26, antibiotic therapy with polymyxin B and amikacin was started to treat Acinetobacter with growth in blood cultures. Sedation was suspended on 7/1 with [person] maintaining a Glasgow coma scale of 3t. [person] presenting with daily fever spikes and requested new infectious screening on 03/07 presented recurrence of tonic seizure with scanning gaze on 04/07, witnessed by the medical team with improvement after 1 ampoule of diazepam. [person] evolves maintaining daily fever spikes and suspected infectious worsening. due to worsening with suspected bloodstream infection, associated with vancomycin in the treatment, [person] evolves with acute kidney injury associated with septic condition use of nephrotoxic medications. performed electroencephalogram on 08/07: findings consistent with asymmetric encephalopathy, which may occur in the context of right hemisphere stroke; on 09/07 spoke with family members about the severity of the case with the assisting team. on the same day, [organization] spoke with family members and opted for palliative care. in the evening [person] evolves with septic shock, evolving to death at {omitted}. I contact {organization}. The on-call physician [person] advises me to fill out the death certificate. On Friday, June 18th, on hemodialysis, [organization] evaluated the catheter and recommended hospitalization at {organization} for replacement and investigation of lower back pain with magnetic resonance imaging and sciatica. He was discharged from {organization} on June 22nd with a schedule to receive a dose of 1000 mg of vancomycin on dialysis. At home, he remained well until Wednesday night, June 23rd, when {person} suddenly noticed unresponsiveness and drowsiness, which prompted him to call emergency medical services. The patient was admitted to the emergency care unit with significant hypotension and blood pressure of 60/40. High doses of norepinephrine were administered. Admission to the emergency unit on June 25 [person] resulted in a decrease in the level of consciousness and hemodynamic instability, requiring high doses of vasoactive drugs, norepinephrine and vasopressin. Orotracheal intubation was required. Meropenem and vancomycin were started. Blood culture collected on admission showed multidrug-resistant Klebsiella. Antibiotics were maintained due to gravity. A computed tomography scan showed a larger bilateral psoas abscess on the left and spondylodiscitis in l2 and l3, contiguous to the psoas abscesses. The abscess was punctured on the left by radiointervention, with growth of multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli. The patient developed fever and blood culture showed multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter. Amikacin was started on July 5. Transthoracic transesophageal echocardiography was performed, without vegetations. [person] showed clinical improvement, and extubation was performed on 07/06. Evaluated by orthopedics, who did not indicate surgical approaches. A new computed tomography scan was performed on 08/02, with puncture of psoas collections bilaterally, with the appearance of hematoma. On 08/06, a Permcath implant was performed for hemodialysis, with precordialgia and dyspnea in the first 30 minutes of dialysis. Evolution: despite the culture showing Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase, [person] showed a good clinical response to meropenem, thus concluding the use of meropenem 1000 mg 1x/day 500 mg post renal replacement therapy for 14 days dated 02/23/2020. He evolved with improvement in infectious parameters, afebrile, with no genitourinary or cardiorespiratory complaints. Latest laboratory tests: Hb: 12.4 ht: 37 platelets: 123 gb: 7.5 without deviation to the left. Undergoing follow-up with nephrology, daily hemodialysis was performed. Schedule: with completion of antibiotic therapy and maintenance of improvement in clinical parameters, discharged from [organization] on 03/09/2020.
